thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need to decide on tier elasticity for the onramp pilot. Customer wants per-route caps + gated features.
kevin: Do they mean hard quotas or throttled feature flags that unlock at volume?
maria: They asked for hard cap on embeddings / second + feature flag to enable "priority inference" above tier.
eli: I'm worried hard caps will lead to support escalations. We could do slot-based reservations instead: customer buys X slots for reserved concurrency.
josh: slots are simpler for ops and map nicely to dedicated pools. But pricing needs to show unit economics.
maria: Exact ask: "allow 2 routes with 50 qps each, extra routes billed at higher per-token rate" — attached doc https://redwood.app/notes/onramp-spec
sana: Can we prototype two options in console? One with soft throttles + UX nudges, one with hard caps + escalation flow.
kevin: Launch criteria: (1) clear billing language, (2) console UX for per-route config, (3) auto-fallback policy for throttled requests, (4) SLOs for priority inference.
eli: Also need an internal migration playbook for customers who exceed soft quotas repeatedly.
maria: Agree. For pricing model, propose: baseline tier includes 100 slot-minutes / month, overage priced per-slot-minute; priority inference is an add-on + 20% markup.
josh: Numbers look ok, but run simulation with customer A/B traces. Also confirm telemetry supports per-route attribution.
sana: I'll mock console UI by Friday and flag where we need backend hooks.
kevin: I'll draft billing copy and legal carveouts for soft vs hard enforcement.
maria: Decision? We implement soft throttles + optional slot reservations as add-on for GA, hard caps only for signed enterprise contracts.
eli: +1. Reduces support load and gives upsell path.
sana: :thumbsup: I'll post prototypes in #product-design when ready.
maria: Thanks team. Ping me if any blockers.
